@Alice Cappo - For MVP, the approach we're going with for suggested prompts on the new tab is to keep them more neutral. "New tab as neutral ground" has been our framing. Then, as I commented below, suggested prompts will be more contextual within the sidebar when a page is in view. 

The current set of "neutral" prompts we're working with is:

Compare tabs
Summarize tabs
Find tabs in history
Write a first draft
Improve writing
Proofread a message
Simplify a topic
Brainstorm ideas
Help make a plan

@Alice Cappo - The suggested prompts that appear when a user is viewing a page will be:
1. more contextual to the page
2. likely longer than one word. 

For example, "Make this vegan" for a recipe or "Summarize the reviews" for a product. Or, for this particular page - a science article - something like "Summarize this" and "Define hominin" might be realistic. For the count, we're currently exploring showing 2 suggested prompts. 

As for the interaction, when these suggested prompts are chosen, the user shouldn't have to do anything else. (Should not have to click the arrow button.) They should be 'one-click'. (The next frame suggests clicking the suggestion will move it into the input area, where the user then has to click enter.) Let me know your thoughts on the 'double-select' idea here and if there's some logic or nuance I'm missing.

@Alice Cappo I still think it’s difficult to distinguish between the classic and smart window states, especially when the user is not on a new tab—see the example below. In our earlier explorations for the smart window, we differentiated not only through color but also through changes in UI shape, which made the distinction between window types more apparent. Since we want to keep the same UI structure across states, color becomes a key differentiator here. With that in mind, it may be worth exploring a slightly stronger color variation.

@Alice Cappo I don’t think a decision is required here, as both states are valid. When the search box is empty, the button appears as an arrow and has kind of disabled state. Once the user starts typing, the label changes to Ask, Search, or Go depending on the detected intent. We infer the intent from the input and update the button accordingly—for example, questions map to Ask, URLs to Go, and so on. Dia follows a similar pattern. In Firefox, however, users also have the ability to change this manually and therefor the button has a dropdown.

3. Entry Points and Discoverability
* Access to Smart Window functionality is currently split across the application menu, tab menu, and contextual actions.

* Recommendation: make switching for smart windows only in the switcher (that will bring your tabs with you from classic window to smart window). However, you can open a new smart window in the application menu.

Color: The dark mode colors are moving in the right direction with the orange and purple (maybe we could go even darker since it’s a dark mode). 

The team is wondering if there is any way to bring purple and orange into light mode and move away from less pick. Exec leadership has not liked pink in the past in the early explorations we’ve done. 

We also change the browser chrome colors for smart window default themes so you do not need to do the same gradient there (which can help make smart window more distinct).

1. Chrome Layout Behavior + Color 
* Detaching the URL bar and shifting chrome behavior in Smart Window introduces complexity that is not needed, and also may be a security concern when sharing a previous pattern early. 
* Recommendation: please stick with the current browser chrome layout and use this option since it indicates the content is coming from the browser.
